headline: Ryan Howard's ninth-inning single walks off the Mets
recap: Trailing 6-5 in the bottom of the ninth, the Phillies rallied against Mets closer Jenrry Mejia. Cody Asche led off with a double and scored the tying run on pinch-hitter Marlon Byrd's single. After two outs, Mejia intentionally walked Chase Utley, and Byrd, who had stolen second during that at-bat, scored the winning run on Ryan Howard's single to right for a 7-6 walk-off win.

Mets starter Zack Wheeler held Philadelphia to three runs over six innings, while Phillies starter Kyle Kendrick was battered for six runs, five earned, on ten hits and two home runs in five innings, leaving the Phillies trailing early.

Relievers Mario Hollands and Jake Diekman combined for three scoreless innings to keep the Phillies within reach, and Ken Giles worked around a hit in the top of the ninth to earn the win. Chase Utley drove in all three of his RBI before the final rally, homering in the first and tripling in the seventh, part of a 3-for-4 night.
